problem_statement: A CoAP message containing an option whose two-byte extended length field, combined with the required length offset, exceeds the 16-bit range is silently accepted: the resulting length wraps instead of the message being rejected, allowing a far larger-than-intended value to be read. Similarly, a block option (Block1 or Block2) whose value is longer than the three bytes a block value can hold is copied into a fixed-size buffer instead of being rejected, and the resulting error is reported as an invalid-argument error rather than a parse error. Both conditions should instead be reported as a parse error so the malformed message is not processed.
oracle_note: observed by validate_instance.py (fail before, pass after the fix); the unit oracle is per executable, so check attribution of the cases to the PR's change
